<subject>Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025</subject>
<body>
My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Supplier Quality Assessment Forms -- provided key legal technology and intellectual capital to rewrite quality assurance forms to be largely consistent with aerospace industry regulatory standards.

2.   Meridian Dynamics and Contract Termination Strategy in the Apex Systems Insolvency -- led legal and procurement team across all Kestrel entities in minimizing Kestrel credit and legal risks. This required an expedited evaluation of Kestrel positions and coordination across Kestrel entities to determine the best possible approach to terminate and then value all Apex Systems contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Policy for Manufacturing -- led the resolution of many critical document retention policy issues and implementation of a new policy across company lines in Kestrel.

4.    Thought Leader on Compliance Risk Management -- continued to develop legal technology for better management and reporting of legal risks across Kestrel. Regulatory tracking and risk ratings are two examples. These legal risk policies have been newly applied in the Bristol facility and Supplier Quality to better evaluate and manage the legal risks in those business units.

5.     Developing New Supply Chains -- integral part in developing new supplier relationships and frameworks by preparing contract forms and formulating new ways to manage legal risks across component manufacturing, fasteners, and composite materials.

6.     Complex Programme Management -- projects having lots of complex issues including the Typhoon retrofit programme, the A400M delivery contracts, Rolls-Royce partnerships, BAE Systems agreements, Airbus supply chain restructuring and Defence Procurement initiatives.

7.     Management -- continued to build a contract-oriented legal team that understand the underlying aerospace businesses.

8.     New Generation of Master Supply Agreements -- taking the lead with industry bodies in developing the next generation of supplier master agreements which would be a single master for all component categories, whether manufactured or sourced. This would reduce the legal work by half.
</body>
